features: A 47.76 m dome only 9 cm thick, with no inner supports, over an octagonal Functionalist market in Algeciras.

why: Czech Cubism is not in the vocabulary; Expressionism is used as the nearest, as the wall's House of the Black Madonna does. Year 1914 from the lead.
name: Bauerova vila
features: The only Cubist villa in the Czech countryside, built in 1912–1914 by Josef Gočár for estate owner Adolf Bauer.

why: Lead names Olbrich's 1901 house and its UNESCO listing; Olbrich's Secession Building is on the wall.
name: Großes Haus Glückert
features: The largest of eight artists' houses built for the 1901 Darmstadt artists' colony exhibition; now a UNESCO site.

why: Year 1953 from the lead; the photo captions say 1952.
name: Stichweh-Wohnhaus
features: Walter Gropius's first postwar building in Germany, and his only one in Hannover.

photos.file: File:Alleehof 4 Hannover Wohnhaus Wilhelm Stichweh Walter Gropius BDA Bund Deutscher Architekten in Niedersachsen.jpg
File:2019 Alleehof 4 in Hannover, Blick auf das Haus Stichweh, Ansicht von Nordwesten.jpg

why: Kept on the architect test (Gočár has two buildings on the wall); the lead is short.
name: Vila Tychonova 4
features: The southern half of a double villa in Prague's Hradčany by Josef Gočár, protected since 1958.

why: Kept on the architect test (Henselmann has three buildings on the wall); the lead is short and gives the Bauhaus link only in the name.
name: Villa Kenwin
features: A Bauhaus-style villa in La Tour-de-Peilz by Hermann Henselmann and Alexander Ferenczy.

why: Kept on the architect test (Michelucci has three buildings on the wall); the lead is short. Regionalism is a judgement from the stone and the photos.
name: Chiesa dei Santi Pietro e Girolamo
features: A church in Pistoia's Collina di Pontelungo, designed by Giovanni Michelucci.

photos.file: File:Pistoia, chiesa dei Santi Pietro e Girolamo a vinacciano, 02.jpg
File:Pistoia, chiesa dei Santi Pietro e Girolamo a vinacciano, interno 07.jpg

why: Kept on the architect test (Mazzoni has a building on the wall). Year 1933 is the inauguration in the lead.
name: Palazzo delle Poste
features: A post office in La Spezia's central Piazza Verdi, designed in its architecture and furnishings by Angiolo Mazzoni.

why: Lead names Brutalism and Stirling and Gowan's first major joint project. Coordinates are missing from prep, so coords is null.
name: Langham House Close
features: Stirling and Gowan's first major joint project: three Grade II* listed blocks, influenced by Le Corbusier.

why: Lead names Johnson and calls it a landmark; the entrance photo is not used as the main photo.
name: WRVA Building
features: Built for a radio station and designed by Philip Johnson, called one of Richmond's most important mid-century landmarks.

why: Lead names Art Nouveau and says the pool was the largest and most modern in the world when finished.
name: Müllersches Volksbad
features: Munich's Art Nouveau public baths, the largest and most modern swimming pool in the world when finished in 1901.

why: Lead names the functionalist style and a plan inspired by Le Corbusier, and says it was once the tallest office building in the country.
name: Dům Radost
features: A 52 m functionalist tower with a cruciform plan inspired by Le Corbusier, once the country's tallest office building.

why: Lead calls it a Constructivist landmark; Constructivism is not in the vocabulary, so Modernism is used. Year 1931 is the end of the 1929–31 build.
name: Communal House of the Textile Institute
features: A Constructivist landmark in Moscow, a 1929–31 student dormitory designed by Ivan Nikolaev for 2,000 students.
commons_category: Category:Communal House of the Textile Institute

why: Pueblo Revival is regional. Year 1936 is the end of the 1934–36 build in the lead.
name: Scholes Hall
features: The first of John Gaw Meem's Pueblo Revival campus buildings, and one of his most notable designs.

why: Lead names Art Deco and Moderne, and says the architect was the school district's main architect.
name: Joseph H. Brown Elementary School
features: A 1937 Philadelphia school by the district's main architect, an exemplar of Art Deco and Moderne design.

why: Lead names Roth, Schubert and Kirchberger; Kirchberger is named for the facade mosaic, so the lead's designers are used. Year 1956 is the end of the 1954–56 build.
name: Hochhaus Württembergische Straße 6
features: West Berlin's first office high-rise, a pioneering example of postwar modernism with open, transparent architecture.

why: Lead names the Case Study Houses programme and the National Register listing; the house is a documented example of it.
name: Case Study House No. 1
features: A single-story house in the Case Study Houses program, completed in 1948 with glass, concrete block and plywood.

photos.file: File:Case Study House No. 1 view from street 2014 (2).jpg
File:Case Study House No. 1 view from street 2014.jpg

why: Kept on the lead's reason (an interesting example of modern church architecture). Year 1964 is from Wikidata; the lead only says the 1960s.
name: Chiesa dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo
features: One of the most interesting examples of modern church architecture in Milan, by Luigi Figini and Gino Pollini.

photos.file: File:Church SS Giovanni and Paolo, Milan.jpg

why: Haiku skipped it for a lead with no reason, but it is a built work by Wiesner (a named well-known modern architect) with excellent whole-building daylight photos; year 1929 from the lead's 1926–1929.
name: Brno Crematorium
features: Arnošt Wiesner's crematorium at Brno Central Cemetery, built to his plans in 1926–1929 on Jihlavská Street.

why: Built work by Wiesner (same standing as Haiku's kept Villa Haas); the lead names him and the 1928–1929 build; clear daylight photos of the whole villa.
name: Villa Neumark
features: Ernst Wiesner's villa for the Brno businessman Walter Neumark, built 1928–1929 as a simpler version of Villa Stiassni.

why: Built work by Fuchs (a named well-known architect); the lead gives him and the 1923–1924 build. Skipped only for a short lead. Photos are corner views through hedge and trees, with no clean full front, so the first is the best of four.
name: Villa Pavlíček
features: The Pavlíček family house in Brno's Masaryk Quarter, designed by Bohuslav Fuchs and built 1923–1924.

photos.file: File:Brno, Stránice, Lerchova, Pavlíčkův rodinný dům (2018-07-21; 01).jpg

why: Haiku kept three other Bartning churches on the same kind of lead; this is the same standing, with four large daylight exterior views. Year 1950 is prep's (the lead gives none). Name uses the lead's own title, since prep's label is a long Commons-style description.
name: Lukaskirche (Worms)
features: A Protestant church in the north of Worms's inner city, by Otto Bartning.

why: Lead names Theodor Fischer as designer and calls the tower the landmark of Pfullingen; built 1905; daylight view of the whole tower.
name: Schönberg Tower
features: A 26.4 m lookout tower from 1905 by the well-known architect Theodor Fischer, a landmark of Pfullingen.

why: Barluzzi's church on the Mount of Olives; lead gives place and the finds made during construction; clear daylight exterior.
name: Dominus Flevit Church
features: A church on the Mount of Olives opposite the Old City walls, where digging uncovered Canaanite artifacts and tombs.

File:Holy Land 2019 (1) P124 Jerusalem Dominus Flevit Church.jpg

why: Lead calls it a modern church in Wiblingen; architect from Wikidata; clear daylight exterior of the whole church.
name: Versöhnungskirche (Ulm)
features: A modern Protestant church in Wiblingen, a district of Ulm.

why: Lead gives NHL status as an important example of 1930s NPS Rustic architecture; the only exterior photo is a black-and-white print.
name: Crater Lake Superintendent's Residence
features: A National Historic Landmark of boulders and heavy woodwork, an important example of 1930s National Park Service Rustic architecture.
